book: Julian of Norwich — Revelations of Divine Love

1: And when I was thirty years old and a half, God sent me a bodily sickness in which I lay for three days and nights, and on the fourth night I received the rites of the church, and the curate set the cross before my face and said: I have brought the image of thy Maker and Saviour. And in that moment my eyes were opened, and I saw the red blood trickle down from under the garland, all hot, flowing in great drops.

But God forbid that you should say or take it so that I am a teacher — for I mean not so, no, I never meant so. For I am a woman, ignorant, feeble, and fretted. And this revelation was made to a simple creature that could no more have told it than a child. But because I am a woman, should I therefore believe that I should not tell you of the goodness of God, since I saw in that same time that it is His will that it be known?

And in this Little Thing I saw three properties. The first is that God made it, the second is that God loveth it, the third, that God keepeth it. But what is to me thereby? Truly the Maker, the Lover, and the Keeper — for till I am substantially oned to Him, I may never have full rest, nor verily know the strength and the bliss of God.
2: It behoved that there should be sin; but all shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well. And here I saw truly that our Lord was never wroth, nor never shall be — for He is God, He is that goodness that all things are made of.

And after this our Lord opened my ghostly eye, and He shewed me the ghostly suffering of His soul. I saw that the longing of God for our love is longer and deeper than all our pain — and that is why He beareth the pain with us, and not against us.
[Revelations, ch. 50 — Thou shalt not be overcome]

And soon the soul was answered by this word and said: Thou shalt not be overcome. And in this our Lord made me to understand that it is His will that we take His behests and His comfortings as largely as we may — for He comforteth readily, and He is our own endless joy.
3: And then our Lord looked into the side of the cross and beheld, and said: Lo me here, God, Thy own handiwork. And I understood: the place of heaven is the soul that is one with God, for He hath made it large enough for all that shall be saved.

And thus was I learned: that our Mother Christ is the very Mother — for in her tender womb the whole world was carried, and from her breasts the soul is fed with grace, and she forgetteth none, from the greatest to the least, and her love faileth never.

Wouldst thou learn thy Lord's meaning in this thing? Learn it well: love was His meaning. Who shewed it thee? Love. What shewed He thee? Love. For what? Love. And after this I saw that He is all thing that is good — and the goodness that every thing hath, it is He.
